title: Risk of gastrointestinal adverse events associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists for weight loss
authors: Sodhi M, Rezaeianzadeh R, Kezouh A, Etminan M
followUp: median 0.6 years on semaglutide, 1.7 years on liraglutide and bupropion-naltrexone; 2006 to June 2020
population: New users with an obesity code and without diabetes in a random sample of 16 million patients from the US PharMetrics Plus claims database: 613 semaglutide, 4144 liraglutide and 654 bupropion-naltrexone users
funder: This study was funded by internal research funds from the Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences, University of British Columbia. The funder had no role in design, conduct, collection, analysis, interpretation, preparation, review or approval of the manuscript, or the decision to submit.
result: Incidence per 1000 person-years for semaglutide, liraglutide and bupropion-naltrexone: biliary disease 11.7 (5 events), 18.6 (162) and 12.6 (16); pancreatitis 4.6 (2), 7.9 (71) and 1.0 (1); bowel obstruction 0, 8.1 (73) and 1.7 (2); gastroparesis 9.1 (4), 7.3 (66) and 3.1 (3). Against bupropion-naltrexone, GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with pancreatitis (adjusted hazard ratio 9.09, 95% CI 1.25 to 66.00), bowel obstruction (4.22, 1.02 to 17.40) and gastroparesis (3.67, 1.15 to 11.90) but not biliary disease (1.50, 0.89 to 2.53). Most events occurred in liraglutide users; BMI was unavailable and E-values were used to assess unmeasured confounding.
